markdown_report:
The next experiment should test **multi-negative discrimination while holding the corrected NextItNet architecture fixed**. At 20% progress, this offers a smaller, more interpretable change than another context-selection module.

Three insights follow from the starting point. First, residual-depth correction preserves the final-state path at initialization. That makes architectural comparisons easier to interpret. Second, reported scores are 0.5325 for residual correction and 0.5175 for direct aggregation. These observations motivate caution about replacing final features, but lack paired uncertainty. Third, sampled training misranking remains 8.22% in Industrial_and_Scientific and 6.67% in Electronics. These are training observations, so stronger discrimination remains a hypothesis rather than an established remedy.

Three literature insights support separate directions. NextItNet permits sampled softmax, and Scalable Cross-Entropy studies informative candidate subsets. Together they motivate testing the objective without replacing causal convolutions. PSL warns about false negatives, while R2NS cautions against early hard mining. Uniform negatives therefore provide a restrained first experiment. MSDCCL distinguishes weighting from deletion. It motivates a later suppression experiment, since depth selection alone cannot remove stale information.

| Direction | Intervention | Unresolved question |
|---|---|---|
| Representation | Residual-depth correction | Are intermediate depths useful? |
| Discrimination | Multi-negative cross-entropy | Does competition improve specific matches? |
| Context | Causal input suppression | Can stale context be reduced safely? |

Scores below are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment includes a positive and negative reason.

| Idea | Scores | Critical assessment |
|---|---|---|
| **Uniform 16-negative cross-entropy** [NextItNet, SCE, PSL] | 2/7/6/8/3 | Originality: controlled adaptation, established loss. Potential: reusable objective, uncertain gains. User: specific recent transitions compete directly, stale context remains. Model: targets misranking, negatives remain uncertain. Difficulty: local loss change, exclusions require care. |
| Same-network hard-negative curriculum [R2NS] | 3/6/6/8/6 | Originality: contextual adaptation, established curriculum. Potential: stronger competitors, false-negative risk. User: challenges broad matches, cannot verify purpose. Model: targets difficult margins, may destabilize training. Difficulty: one network suffices, retrieval adds cost. |
| Causal convolution-input suppression [MSDCCL] | 4/7/8/6/6 | Originality: family-specific placement, familiar gating. Potential: adaptable context, useful history may disappear. User: targets stale and broad associations, intent remains latent. Model: may improve discrimination, diagnosis supplies no temporal evidence. Difficulty: localized gates, substantial masking checks. |

Select the first idea. It explicitly targets broad relatedness displacing specific current matches and older secondary interests outranking recent-purpose matches by training the existing causal representation against multiple alternatives. This connection is indirect and must be tested; the loss introduces no forgetting mechanism. It also targets measured sampled misranking. Keep depth aggregation unchanged, exclude known training positives, and select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10. Compatibility, quantity suitability, and duplication remain unresolved.

idea.description: Replace the supplied corrected NextItNet's training objective with cross-entropy over one positive and 16 uniformly sampled negatives per valid causal position. Keep its backbone, existing depth aggregation configuration, scoring head, optimizer, and inference architecture unchanged. Train exactly one independent model per category, with no auxiliary scorer or checkpoint averaging.
idea.motivation: The hypothesis is that explicit competition among multiple alternatives improves conditional next-item discrimination. This addresses two user-facing failures as testable hypotheses: broad associations displacing specific matches to current purpose, and older secondary interests outranking matches supported by recent interactions. The latter connection is indirect: the objective can reward use of recent predictive evidence, but does not enforce forgetting. The model-facing target is sampled training misranking, observed at 8.22% in Industrial_and_Scientific and 6.67% in Electronics. Neither these measurements nor the historical proposal scores establish that the proposed loss improves held-out HR@10. Retain causal input suppression as a separate future hypothesis rather than combining interventions.
idea.implementation_notes:
This is an integration component because the supplied baseline train.py and predictor writer are not included in the prompt. Integrate it into that baseline rather than reconstructing its data formats or training harness. The comparison starts from the host-supplied corrected cold start, never another trial's checkpoint. Keep the current architecture, including whichever depth-correction configuration the host supplies, identical between the original-loss control and this loss experiment. Do not silently import an architecture from the inspiration history.

Use M=16 and temperature=1.0 as one prespecified configuration. Do not simultaneously sweep negative count, temperature, architecture, and optimizer. Sample negatives uniformly without replacement from mapped, training-observed items excluding padding, the position's target, and every item in that user's permitted training history. Use only training histories for these exclusions; do not inspect validation or test interactions. Excluding future positions within a user's training partition is an explicit retrospective sampling convention, not a causal input feature. It prevents known-positive collisions but does not resolve latent relevance. If the eligible pool has fewer than 16 items, use all eligible items and mask the remaining slots. If it is empty, skip that position and count it. Do not manufacture a negative or loop indefinitely.

The code below deliberately separates negative sampling from the differentiable loss. Implement the sampler in the baseline's existing CPU sampling workers, using an independent seed-42 random stream so additional negative draws do not change the sequence sampler's stream. Rejection sampling with per-user training-history sets is suitable for ordinary pools; use an explicit eligible complement when rejection becomes inefficient or the pool is small. Do not cache a user-by-catalog dense matrix. Record actual negative counts and skipped positions. Negatives have shape N x 16 after valid-position filtering, with zero used only for masked slots.

Compute scores through the same model.predict_score implementation used by diagnosis and inference, preserving its item bias or transformations if any. Do not substitute raw dot products unless that is exactly the baseline scorer. The helper receives positive and negative scores to avoid assuming an unsupported broadcasting contract. Average the loss over eligible valid positions. Keep the baseline's explicit regularization unchanged; replace only its data-loss term. Temperature stays fixed at 1.0, and no log-sampling correction is applied: this is a sampled candidate-classification objective, not a claimed unbiased estimator of full-catalog cross-entropy. Its training candidate distribution differs from the host evaluator's fixed validation candidates.

Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four category routes, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], single-GPU execution, at most 200 epochs, and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Preserve the SASREC_EPOCHS default of 200 and cap it at 200. Write checkpoints, configurations, and diagnostics only beneath the trial directory. Keep the baseline checkpoint inspection and stopping schedule identical across eligible comparisons, and record exact inherited hyperparameters. Count diagnostics, failed attempts, and all prior expenditure against the shared 43,200 GPU-second budget. The prompt does not supply remaining allowance or timing, so budget feasibility cannot be certified here. Do not rank an incomplete configuration missing any category.

Inference requires no new layer: preserve the predictor writer's exact model definition, reconstruct the saved architecture configuration, and strict-load one state_dict for the routed category. Save objective and negative-sampling settings as training metadata without introducing an inference-time dependency. Verify score agreement after save/load. Continue gathering the largest nonzero sequence index for left-padded histories, with the baseline's empty-history convention; never gather count-1. Preserve causal masking and the existing log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), and ModelView interfaces.

Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions, and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). The loader retains its existing (None, sequence, positive, negative) B x L contract; the training-only multi-negative sampler need not change it. Use fixed diagnostic negatives across compared models rather than diagnosing with each model's changing training negatives. Report sampled misranking and negative counts with definitions. Training margins, representation rank, and prefix perturbations are descriptive mechanism probes, not held-out ranking improvements. Existing structural graph analysis remains valid only if the architecture is unchanged and recognized.

Select solely by the unchanged pinned four-category macro validation HR@10, preferring the original-loss control on exact ties. Treat the simulator's twenty training users as qualitative feedback; do not create an auxiliary selection score. If paired validation outcomes are supplied by the host, report paired category differences and conditional user-bootstrap uncertainty; otherwise state that paired uncertainty is unavailable. No evaluator changes, hidden test access, extra metadata, pretrained weights, hard mining, separately fitted popularity scores, or model fusion are introduced.
idea.pseudocode:
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F


def multi_negative_cross_entropy(positive_scores, negative_scores,
                                 negative_valid, temperature=1.0):
    """Training-only candidate classification for valid causal positions.

    positive_scores: (N,), produced by the unchanged model scorer.
    negative_scores: (N, M), produced by that same scorer.
    negative_valid: (N, M), bool; False denotes a padded candidate slot.
    Returns (mean_loss, number_of_eligible_positions).
    """
    if temperature <= 0:
        raise ValueError('temperature must be positive')
    if positive_scores.ndim != 1 or negative_scores.ndim != 2:
        raise ValueError('Expected positive (N,) and negative (N,M)')
    if negative_scores.shape[0] != positive_scores.shape[0]:
        raise ValueError('Position counts disagree')
    if negative_valid.shape != negative_scores.shape:
        raise ValueError('Negative mask shape disagrees')
    if negative_valid.dtype != torch.bool:
        raise TypeError('negative_valid must be boolean')

    eligible = negative_valid.any(dim=1)
    count = int(eligible.sum().item())
    if count == 0:
        # Caller skips the optimizer step if the whole batch is ineligible.
        return positive_scores.sum() * 0.0, 0

    pos = positive_scores[eligible].float().unsqueeze(1)
    neg = negative_scores[eligible].float()
    mask = negative_valid[eligible]
    neg = neg.masked_fill(~mask, float('-inf'))
    logits = torch.cat((pos, neg), dim=1) / temperature
    labels = torch.zeros(count, dtype=torch.long, device=logits.device)
    return F.cross_entropy(logits, labels), count

originality.positive: Provides a narrowly controlled objective experiment within the required NextItNet family and existing diagnostic interfaces.
originality.negative: Multi-negative cross-entropy is established, and NextItNet already supports sampled-softmax objectives; benchmark application adds little methodological novelty.

future_potential.positive: Can establish whether candidate discrimination merits further study before spending budget on architecture changes or hard-negative curricula.
future_potential.negative: Uniform negatives may remain easy, false negatives persist, and the objective does not directly suppress stale context or establish practical compatibility.

code_difficulty.positive: Changes the training loss and sampler while preserving the backbone, deployed scorer, and checkpoint architecture.
code_difficulty.negative: Efficient per-user exclusions, reproducible sampler streams, scorer shape compatibility, and small-pool handling require careful integration.

related_work.title: NextItNet
contributions: Introduces causal dilated convolutional next-item modeling.
Supports sampled-softmax training as an alternative to full-catalog softmax.
limitations: Does not establish that this proposed 16-negative configuration improves the pinned benchmark.
Causal convolution alone does not identify current purchasing purpose.

related_work.title: Scalable Cross-Entropy (RecSys 2024)
contributions: Studies efficient softmax approximation using informative catalog subsets.
limitations: Its informative-subset method differs from the proposed uniform sampler.
Reported results do not demonstrate gains for this NextItNet task.

related_work.title: PSL (NeurIPS 2024)
contributions: Examines false-negative sensitivity and alternative pairwise activations.
limitations: Excluding observed positives does not eliminate uncertain relevance among unobserved items.
Does not validate the proposed objective on the supplied benchmark.

related_work.title: R2NS (WWW 2026)
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-up before curriculum-controlled hard-negative retrieval.
limitations: Retrieval and hardness schedules add complexity beyond this initial experiment.
Hard negatives can include relevant unobserved items.

related_work.title: MSDCCL (2024)
contributions: Combines soft weighting and hard denoising to address noisy sequential context.
limitations: Weighting may retain irrelevant context, while deletion may remove useful history.
Does not establish that the supplied model's errors arise from stale context.
